title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Settlers beat EU diplomats in West Bank
preheader: Belgium wants EU sanctions as Rubio warns of a crisis before Israel's vote.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Sunday, October 18, 2026 — the 2 stories that matter most today, plus 2 updates on stories you're following and 6 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats in the West Bank
stories.why_important: Israeli settlers attacked a convoy of European diplomats and beat a visiting French mayor during the Palestinian olive harvest. Belgium says it will push for EU sanctions on those responsible. Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned of a West Bank crisis ahead of Israel's October 27 election.
stories.what_overlooked: US officials say settlers have made at least 170 attacks on Palestinians since September 27, a pace previous olive harvests rarely saw.
stories.prediction: Whether EU foreign ministers start formal sanctions talks this week will show if Belgium's push has real backing.

stories.story_title: France's cost-of-living protests turn into riots and looting
stories.why_important: Hundreds of thousands marched over living costs and school conditions, and the unrest became France's worst riots in years. Protesters burned Limoges town hall and looted shops, and police detained about 1,200 people months before the election to replace Macron.
stories.what_overlooked: US Vice President JD Vance blamed immigration for the unrest, but French officials have not repeated that claim.
stories.prediction: Whether unions call another national march this week will show if the protest wave is still growing.

quick_hits.text: Pope Leo XIV left Rome's Gemelli Hospital and returned to the Vatican four days after surgery for lung cancer.
Across the US, 'No Kings' organizers held rallies urging early voting in the November 3 midterm elections that will decide control of Congress.
Four people died fighting Indonesia's wildfires, and Singapore's leader vowed legal action against companies behind the haze choking Southeast Asia.
Vietnam signed a free trade deal with the four-nation European Free Trade Association to cut duties on industrial, fish and farm goods, CNA reported.
A Chinese facility in Laos is forcing Vietnam to compete for influence in Vientiane on economics rather than history, the Lowy Institute argued.
Egypt's President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi said his term will end in 2030 and the constitution will not be amended to extend it.

big_number.context: Kenya's confirmed Ebola cases, up from three a day earlier, now include three health workers who treated the first patient.
